header: Package & Product Category — Reference & Data Cleanup
rows: One tab per source table, plus a Data Cleanup tab with a focused column set for review. Table identities below were corrected after cross-checking sample queries against the data - see the note at the bottom on products_packages_products.

The master table of coach/consultation packages sold on the platform. One row per package (id). Holds package identity (internal_name, external_name + Arabic variants), pricing (currency, retail_price, final_price, discount_type/value), status (is_active), categorization (product_category_id -> product_category.id, internal_category), consultation_type, SEO fields (seo_url, meta_title/description, keywords), content fields (description_en/ar, disclaimer, dha_license), partner/coach linkage (associate_coach_id, partner_id, external_partner_id), and country scoping (country_id).

Per-city pricing and SLA configuration for a package: pricing (retail_price, final_price, discount_type/value), delivery and SLA commitments (coach_sla, delivery_time, operations_sla, order_sla), and status, keyed by coach_consultation_package_id (-> coach_consultation_package.id) and city_id. (Corrected: this tab was previously mislabeled products_packages_products - confirmed via `id = 74` lookup queries that the real products_packages_products table is something else entirely; see below.)

Join table mapping a package to its secondary categories (confirmed via `coach_consultation_package_id = 138`, which has 5 rows here - a package can belong to more than one secondary category). Only 22 of 175 packages currently have an entry. secondary_categories_id is a foreign key into product_category.id (see next row).

Lookup table of product categories shown on the platform (id, name, title + Arabic variants, description, location, position_value, status/is_deleted, country_id, internal_category, is_mini_packages_included). Referenced by both coach_consultation_package.product_category_id AND coach_consultation_packages_secondary_categories.secondary_categories_id. CONFIRMED IDENTICAL to products_packages_products: a direct query for products_packages_products ids [16,19,26,31,45,46,55,57,74,83,86,88,92,98,107,108] returned the exact same id/name/title/description values as this table - same columns, same data. products_packages_products is not a separate table; it is this table.

One row per package_id from coach_consultation_package, with: internal_name, external_name, countryId, is_active, product_category_id, internal_category, consultation_type (all from coach_consultation_package), secondary_categories_id (from coach_consultation_packages_secondary_categories, comma-separated where a package has more than one; blank where none set - only 22 of 175 packages currently have at least one), and products_packages_products.name (the matching category name(s) for those secondary_categories_id values, looked up in product_category - since products_packages_products IS product_category).

An earlier version of this workbook mislabeled the per-city pricing data as products_packages_products, based on a coincidental id match (id=74 happened to exist in both). Sample queries against the real products_packages_products table (ids 26, 19, 74, 88, 108) showed it returns category-style rows (name='Newborn care and Babysitting', 'Women Health', etc.) - a direct match to product_category. That table has been corrected here and secondary_categories_id names are now populated from it.
